tldr: DeepSeek open-sourced DeepInfer on Oct 20, the inference software behind its production models, first framed as a way to cut AI operating costs and then as pressure on OpenAI and Anthropic. Oct 21 coverage added the 155T tokens-a-day serving scale and a high serving margin.
whats_new: Nov 2: TechNode, TNGlobal and Help Net Security describe DeepSeek's dsh-superagent as a proactive research prototype, a coding agent that watches team chats for work.
why_it_matters: Two open DeepSeek releases in two weeks, a serving stack and a coding-agent architecture, give platform teams reference designs to benchmark their own inference and agent harness against.

status.detail: DeepInfer is public and unreproduced; dsh-superagent is described as a research prototype with no independent results yet.

beats.headline: Earlier adjacent items clustered before the release
beats.summary: Not DeepSeek coverage: a web-agent distillation paper (Oct 14) and a mixed-hardware inference framework (Oct 18).

beats.headline: DeepSeek ties V4.1-Flash-1017 to its own Harness (Oct 17)
beats.summary: Groundwork for the later Harness-team releases.

beats.headline: DeepSeek open-sources the stack that runs its models
beats.summary: Bloomberg, Quartz, Gizmodo and PYMNTS report the release on Oct 20 as an open-source tool to lower AI operating costs.

beats.headline: SiliconANGLE names it DeepInfer, the framework behind production services
Scale and margin figures arrive
beats.summary: Latent Space and follow-up writeups cite 155T tokens a day and a high-margin serving business.

beats.headline: DeepSeek's Harness team open-sources dsh-superagent, a router-worker coding agent
beats.summary: Hacker News links the GitHub architecture on Oct 31; Nov 1 coverage frames it as a challenge to Claude Code; Nov 2 reports call it a proactive research prototype that watches team chats.

beats.headline: Later unrelated items in the window
beats.summary: Not DeepSeek coverage: llm-d 1.0 (Oct 20), agent, evaluation, multi-agent, compression and retrieval papers (Oct 21-Nov 2), inference-engine essays and demos (Oct 24, Oct 31, Nov 2, Nov 3), and a quantization paper (Oct 29).

open_questions: Does an independent benchmark reproduce the 155T tokens/day and ~80% margin figures?
Which license terms govern commercial reuse of DeepInfer and dsh-superagent?
Does dsh-superagent's bug-fixing claim hold on an independent coding benchmark?
Does dsh-superagent run on models other than DeepSeek's own?
take_for_builders: Read the DeepInfer and dsh-superagent repos and licenses before borrowing designs; treat the margin and bug-fixing claims as unverified until someone reproduces them outside DeepSeek's stack.
